title: Robichaux's personnel and the open-air dance
summary: Robichaux's players, an all-reading repertoire, and the afternoon lawn dance followed by an evening hall dance.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Well, that'd be around about, say around about 4.30. What kind of a badge did Roebelshowe have? Oh, Joe Roebelshowe, yeah, full badge. He had himself, Varon. He had Jim Williams' trumpet. He had Bat De Lille, trombone. He had George Barquet, clarinet. He had Bud Scott, guitar.
Bud would sing with the band too, wouldn't he, sometimes?
Sometimes Bud would sing. He sure would. And he had Henry Kimball bass violin, and Louis Contrall was drummer. That's his band.
What kind of music did they play? Hmm? What kind of music did they play?
Well, they played all like Scott Joplin and all that. Were they reading all the time?
Oh, they didn't do nothing but read.
Only read.
Only read.
Only read. No ad libbing. No at all. Only read. Nothing but read. Only one number they played by air was home sweet home. That ends the program. That ends the program.
That ends the program. But then there was a hall in the-

Now, when they played, they played from four, four till seven. Then, all the people, a lot of them would stay, and a lot of them was coming for the night dance, a lot of them remained. Then they'd tear that hour, they'd go in lunch up, eight o'clock, they'd start to dance in the hall. And they played.
First they played in the open air.
In the open air. Just out on the lawn?
Yeah, out on the lawn. No bandstand or anything?
Only time they didn't go out in the lawn was the weather was bad. Yes. That would knock it out. But mostly it was all nice weather.
Then there was a dance hall too, huh?
Oh yeah, a dance hall right from out along the big old hall. Big dance hall. And that left me to the fourth.
When they played out in the open, did people dance or they'd sit around on the grass?
Oh no, they danced. Where'd they dance? They danced right out on the ground. Oh, that place was fine.
Was it nice grass or was it-
No, they had canvas all around it too. I see. Sure. Fine place. Tables or anything?
Oh yeah, that table. Could you get a beer or-
Oh, all you want there. All you want.
Sure. What did they have, a little stand and sort of a bar?
They had a little bar on the side. A little top over it, you know. Beer stacked high in this ceiling. Kegs? Keg beer. Sure.
